gaps.root_cause: --python is passed through unresolved; dependencies._python_installed runs it with cwd set to a probe directory

gaps.test_after: pass: relative .venv path exit 0 with the dependency report; missing path, directory or unknown name: exit 2 with a message, no traceback
gaps.negative_controls: absolute path unchanged; a path with spaces resolves

gaps.root_cause: classify_command keeps the runner_args of the first recognized segment only
gaps.expected: every runner invocation in a multi-line run step counts as a CI scope; a suite no line runs is still a gap; line order does not change the result
gaps.observed: only the first unittest line of a step is a scope: false high CI_TEST_EXECUTION_GAP; swapping the lines moves the false gap

gaps.negative_controls: only-a keeps the gap for b/tests; an unresolved `cd $VAR` claims nothing
gaps.metrics: classify_command records every recognized command of a step (tool, args, directory after a literal cd); ci.py builds one scope per command
gaps.limitations: scopes stay DECLARED (bash -e stops at the first failing line: a later line is only conditionally reached); GitLab/Azure use the same command table but their working directories are still not read

gaps.root_cause: _self_referential and _determinism read the same two-call pattern differently
gaps.expected: `a = f(x); assert a == f(x)` is the same weak determinism oracle as `assert f(x) == f(x)`, not a false green
gaps.observed: assigned form: FALSE_GREEN SELF_REFERENTIAL_ORACLE; direct form: WEAK_ORACLE DETERMINISM
gaps.test_before: tests/test_dogfood_calibration.py AXF-03 test fails on 0.10.0; tests/test_effectiveness.py pinned the old SELF_REFERENTIAL reading and was updated (contract change)
gaps.test_after: pass: direct and assigned forms are both the weak DETERMINISM oracle (WEAK_ORACLE candidate, never FALSE_GREEN)
gaps.negative_controls: a contract value, another input, a reassigned name, an action between the two calls: VALUE
gaps.limitations: Python only: JavaScript/JVM still read call==call as TAUTOLOGY and the assigned form as SELF_REFERENTIAL (DG-0101-09)

gaps.root_cause: any handler whose body is pass counts as swallowing, whatever it catches
gaps.expected: `except (ErrA, ErrB): pass` around the subject is a limited typed-error oracle (another exception fails the test); `except Exception: pass` stays a swallowed exception
gaps.observed: typed handler reported as FALSE_GREEN SWALLOWED_EXCEPTION, the same as `except Exception` (the Engine saw NO_ASSERTION on a Hypothesis variant)
gaps.test_before: tests/test_dogfood_calibration.py AXF-06 tests fail on 0.10.0 (typed handler: SWALLOWED_EXCEPTION false green; assertion kind NO_ASSERTION)
gaps.test_after: pass: TYPED_ERROR_BOUNDARY assertion kind, TYPED_ERROR weak oracle; Hypothesis variant read the same way
gaps.negative_controls: except Exception, except AssertionError, and a typed handler around an assertion stay SWALLOWED_EXCEPTION
gaps.limitations: the oracle says only that no other exception escapes; it is weak (smoke-like) by design. The Engine's KeyError negative control was not re-run (Engine code not executed here)

gaps.root_cause: the redundancy key ignores which module the body's names come from

gaps.metrics: TestFacts.subjects (project files the test's imported names resolve to) is part of the redundancy key; self-audit 18.8 s vs 17.4-18.7 s on 0.10.0
gaps.limitations: Python only; names reached through fixtures, conftest or attribute chains on other objects are not resolved. Portfolio registration of AXF-07 is CP4

gaps.origin: agent, from the M1 attribution list (a pipeline that masked a verifier's exit code was found by the agent, not by Assertiva) and the GitHub Actions shell documentation
gaps.source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax (accessed 2026-11-01): unspecified shell on Linux is `bash -e {0}`; explicit `bash` adds `-o pipefail`
gaps.expected: a declared CI step that discards the test command's exit status is reported
gaps.observed: 0.10.0 reported nothing: the agent had to find such pipelines itself
gaps.test_after: pass: CI_TEST_STATUS_MASKED (medium) for `| tee` in the default Linux shell and for `|| true` / `|| echo` / `|| exit 0` in any shell
gaps.negative_controls: explicit `shell: bash`, `set -o pipefail`, a Windows runner, a matrix-chosen runner (not decided), a pipe after a non-test command, `|| exit 1`
gaps.metrics: no finding on the Framework, the Engine, Assertiva or the two third-party repositories (none pipes its tests: no false positive, and no real-world positive either)
gaps.limitations: GitHub Actions decides the pipe case (its shell semantics are adapter knowledge); `|| true` is read for every provider. Windows (pwsh) pipelines are not decided

ideas.idea: Optional advisory lookup for --dependencies (OSV / pip-audit / npm audit), network and opt-in
ideas.why: no consumer inside an audit yet; inventory already says vulnerabilities are UNKNOWN and names OSV-Scanner to reuse

ideas.idea: Budget-aware mutation sharding (AXO-M2-03): run a large module in traceable shards under the budget
ideas.why: must keep the full planned population as denominator; needs a design that cannot game the score

ideas.idea: Portable feedback intake manifest (import AXF/AFB lineage from dogfood PRs)
ideas.why: the JSON intakes plus `portfolio feedback add` cover the current single consumer

ideas.idea: Ingest Engine SARIF as untrusted candidate evidence (AXO-M2-08)
ideas.why: would add a second source of truth without a consumer in an audit

ideas.idea: Shared test helper for four similar tests/*::_run helpers
ideas.why: they drive different tools and keep fixture independence; merging saves little and couples them

ideas.idea: Read the provider's documented shell semantics to decide whether a piped test step can fail (pipefail)
ideas.source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax (accessed 2026-11-01): unspecified shell `bash -e {0}`, explicit bash `-eo pipefail`, Windows pwsh
ideas.why: implemented as CI_TEST_STATUS_MASKED (DG-0101-11) for GitHub Actions; other providers only for `|| true`-style forms until their defaults are verified

ideas.idea: Treat unittest exit 5 / zero executed tests as never-passing in every reproduced part
ideas.why: the declared plan (AXF-05) keeps an empty part UNKNOWN; consistent with the adapter's existing single-run rule

ideas.idea: Process-level confinement (container/VM) for running untrusted project code; venv or RestrictedPython are not sandboxes
ideas.source: https://github.com/zopefoundation/RestrictedPython README (states it is not a sandbox); OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 LLM01/LLM06 https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/ (accessed 2026-11-01)
ideas.why: the Skill now refuses to call a copy or venv a sandbox (AXF-08); real confinement is the existing roadmap item (EXECUTION_SECURITY residual risk 1), not a patch-release change

ideas.idea: Per-mutant identity and a complete survivor record as the unit of review (as cross-tool survivor triage formats do: file, line, mutator, original, mutated)
ideas.source: Cosmic Ray docs https://cosmic-ray.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ (no equivalence marker; survivors triaged by people); tessl.io mutant-survival-triage (third-party skill, not a standard) (accessed 2026-11-01)
ideas.why: survivor_sites is complete with mutant_id and status (AXF-04); reviewing scope by an explicit list of ids is the next step if assessments need it

ideas.idea: Assessment scope given as reviewed mutant ids instead of a number
ideas.why: the count check closes the reported defect; a list of ids would let the engine say which mutants stay unreviewed, worth it once an agent consumer asks for it
